source.title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields

accepted.question_text: Let G be a connected semisimple Lie group, Γ an irreducible lattice in G, and A a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup of G with dim A > 1. Is every C^1-small perturbation of the action of A on G/Γ C^∞-conjugate to an action of A defined by a continuous homomorphism from A to the centralizer of A in G?
accepted.context_brief: Local rigidity for split Cartan subgroup actions

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 1. Let G be a connected semisimple Lie group, Γ an irreducible lattice in G, and A a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup of G with dim A > 1. Then any C 1-small perturbation of the action of A on G /Γ is C ∞ -conjugate to the action of A deﬁned by a continuous homomorphism from A to the c entralizer of A in G.

accepted.question_text: In the setting where G is a connected semisimple Lie group, Γ is an irreducible lattice in G, A is a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup D of G with dim A > 1, and A is not contained in a wall of a Weyl chamber of D, is every C^1-small perturbation of the action of A on G/Γ C^∞-conjugate to an action of A defined by a continuous homomorphism from A to D?
accepted.context_brief: Local rigidity away from Weyl chamber walls

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 2. If in Conjecture 1 the group A is not contained in a wall of a Weyl chamber of the split Cartan subgroup D, then any C 1-small perturbation of the action of A on G /Γ is C ∞ -conjugate to the action of A deﬁned by a continuous homomorphism from A to D.

accepted.question_text: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism topologically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism on an infranilmanifold?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 3. Every Anosov diffeomorphism is topologically conjugate to a hy-perbolic automorphism on an infranilmanifold.

accepted.question_text: Is every irreducible Anosov action of Z^k or R^k, with k ≥ 2, C^∞-conjugate to an algebraic action?
accepted.context_brief: Global rigidity of irreducible higher-rank Anosov actions

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 4. Every “irreducible” Anosov Zk - and Rk -action, k ≥ 2, is C ∞ -con-jugate to an algebraic action.

accepted.question_text: Is every action of a connected semisimple Lie group whose simple factors all have real rank at least 2, or of a lattice in such a group, that contains an element acting nontrivially and uniformly partially hyperbolically C^∞-conjugate to an algebraic action?
accepted.context_brief: Global rigidity of higher-rank semisimple actions

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 5. Every action of a connected semisimple Lie group of higher ra nk (i.e., all simple factors have real rank at least 2) or a lattice in it that has an element which acts non-trivially uniformly partially hyperbolically, is C∞ -conjugate to an algebraic action.

accepted.question_text: Do measure-rigidity results for higher-rank abelian group actions produce obstructions to smooth or continuous irreducible actions of a higher-rank abelian group on a compact manifold?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 6 (D. Fisher) . Do the new results on measure rigidity for actions of higher rank abelian groups give rise to obstructions to smoo th or continuous irre-ducible actions of a higher rank abelian group on a compact ma nifold?

accepted.question_text: For multiplicatively independent positive integers m and n, are the only probability Borel measures on R/Z that are ergodic under the semigroup generated by multiplication by m and multiplication by n the Lebesgue measure and finite-support measures?
accepted.context_brief: Furstenberg measure rigidity on the circle

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 7 (H. Furstenberg [88]) . Let m and n be multiplicatively indepen-dent positive integers. Then the only probability Borel measures on R/Z which are ergodic under the action of the semigroup generated by multi plications by m and n are the Lebesgue measure and measures with ﬁnite support.

accepted.question_text: For an algebraic Anosov action of R^k or Z^k, k ≥ 2, on a biquotient M of a connected Lie group G, and for an ergodic probability Borel measure μ on M, must either μ be a finite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures on closed subgroups of G, or must supp μ fiber equivariantly over a manifold N on which the action reduces to rank one?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 8 (A. Katok, R. Spatzier [128]) . Let M be a manifold which is a biquotient of a connected Lie group G. Given an algebraic Ano sov action of Rk or Zk , k ≥ 2, on M and an ergodic probability Borel measure µ on M , one of the following holds: (i) The measure µ is a ﬁnite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures supported on closed subgroups of G. (ii) The support of µ ﬁbers over a manifold N in an equivariant way such that the action on N reduces to a rank one action.

accepted.question_text: Let A′ be the ring of adeles formed by taking the product over a subset of places of Q, and let Γ be an irreducible lattice in SL(2,A′). What are the finite ergodic D(A′)-invariant measures on SL(2,A′)/Γ, where D is the diagonal subgroup in SL(2)?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 9 (E. Lindenstrauss) . Let A′ be deﬁned as the ring of adeles, but the product is taken over a subset of places of Q and Γ an “irreducible” lattice in SL(2, A′). What are the ﬁnite ergodic D (A′)-invariant measures on SL(2, A′)/Γ?

accepted.question_text: Can the measure-rigidity results for unipotent flows be extended to the adelic setting?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 10 (L. Silberman). Extend the results on measure rigidity of unipotent ﬂows to the adelic setting.

accepted.question_text: Suppose H acts on a space X preserving a geometric structure, and P is a parabolic subgroup in the ambient setting. Under what conditions on X is every finite P-invariant measure H-invariant; equivalently, which H-actions are stiff?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 11 (E. Lindenstrauss) . Suppose that H acts on a space X preserving some geometric structure. Under what conditions on X is ever y ﬁnite P -invariant measure H -invariant? In other words, which H -actions are stiff (see [89])?

accepted.question_text: For a noncompact semisimple Lie group G of rank one, a discrete subgroup Γ of G, and a horospherical subgroup U of G, what are the U-ergodic Radon measures on G/Γ? In particular, are they all either carried by closed U-orbits or obtained from the harmonic-function construction?
accepted.context_brief: Horospherical Radon measures in rank one

evidence.quote: QUESTION 12 (F . Ledrappier, O. Sarig). Let G be a noncompact semisimple Lie group of rank one, Γ a discrete subgroup of G, and U a horospherical subgroup of G. What are the U -ergodic Radon measures on G /Γ? In particular , are they either carried by closed U -orbits or given by the harmonic function construction?

accepted.question_text: If Γ is a normal conilpotent subgroup of a uniform lattice in SL(2,R), is the Haar measure nonsquashable, meaning that the centralizer of the horocycle flow does not contain an invertible nonsingular transformation that fails to preserve the measure?

evidence.quote: A ut -invariant measure µ is called squashable if the centralizer of ut contains an invertible nonsingular transformation that does not pre serve µ. QUESTION 13 (F . Ledrappier, O. Sarig). Let Γ be a normal conilpotent subgroup of a uniform lattice in SL(2, R). Is the Haar measure nonsquashable?

accepted.question_text: For either a large subgroup Γ of the automorphism group of a finite-volume nilmanifold, or a large subgroup Γ of a Lie group acting by translations on G/Λ where Λ is a lattice in G, are the only ergodic Γ-invariant probability measures those supported on finite Γ-orbits and Haar measure?
accepted.context_brief: Invariant measures for large algebraic group actions

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 14 (A. Furman). Consider one of the following actions of a group Γ: 1. Γ is a “large” (e.g., Zariski dense) subgroup of the group of au tomorphisms of a nilmanifold of ﬁnite volume. 2. Γ is a “large” subgroup of a Lie group acting by translations on G/Λ, where Λ is a lattice in G. Then the only ergodic Γ-invariant probability measures are the measures sup-ported on ﬁnite Γ-orbits and the Haar measure.

accepted.question_text: For an Anosov flow on a compact Riemannian manifold whose stable bundle has an invariant splitting and fast stable foliation W^s_+, what are the invariant ergodic measures for W^s_+?

evidence.quote: The distribution E s + integrates to the fast stable foliation W s + . The following is a nonlinear analog of the Ragunathan’ s ques tion about clas-siﬁcations of measures invariant under unipotent ﬂows: QUESTION 15 (F . Ledrappier). Describe the invariant ergodic measures for the fast stable foliation W s + .

accepted.question_text: Let G be a Lie group, Γ a lattice in G, U={u(t)} a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup, and x∈G/Γ with dense Ux. Can one prove equidistribution in G/Γ of {u(t_n)x} when t_n is [n^α] for α>1, [P(n)] for a polynomial P, or the nth prime number?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 16 (G. Margulis [174]). Prove equidistribution of the sequence{u(tn)x} in G/Γ, where t n is one of the following: 1. tn = [nα]3 for α > 1, 2. tn = [P (n)], where P (x) is a polynomial, 3. tn is the n-th prime number .

accepted.question_text: Let V be a connected Ad-unipotent subgroup of a Lie group G, Γ a lattice in G, and x∈G/Γ with dense Vx. For a good sequence of subsets A_n⊂V and every f∈C_c(G/Γ), do the normalized Haar averages of f(vx) over A_n converge to the Haar probability integral on G/Γ with an effective error term?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 17 (G. Margulis [174]). Show that for a “good” sequence of subsets An ⊂ V and every f ∈ Cc (G/Γ), limn→∞ 1 Vol(An) ∫ An f (v x) d v = ∫ G/Γ f d µ with effective error term, where d v is a Haar measure on V , and µ is the Haar probability measure on G/Γ.

accepted.question_text: Let L be a Lie group, G a closed subgroup, Λ a lattice in L, a∈G semisimple with expanding horospherical subgroup U, x0∈L/Λ with dense Gx0, γ:[0,1]→U analytic, and ν the pushforward of Lebesgue measure under t↦γ(t)x0. What condition on γ ensures that a^nν converges to Haar measure λ on L/Λ as n→∞?

evidence.quote: Take any analytic curve γ : [0, 1] → U , and let ν be the image of the Lebesgue measure on [0, 1] under the map t /mapstoc〈ar→γ(t )x0. QUESTION 18 (N. Shah). Under what condition on γ does a nν → λ as n → ∞ ?

accepted.question_text: Does Shah's equidistribution result for L=SO(m,1) and G=SO(n,1), m>n, hold for all Lie groups L containing G=SO(n,1)?
accepted.context_brief: Shah curve equidistribution for larger Lie groups

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 19 (N. Shah). The same result holds for all Lie groups L containing G = SO(n, 1).

accepted.question_text: For a semisimple Lie group G acting on a real normed vector space V, a point p∈V with finite stabilizer, R_T={g∈G: ||gp||<T}, a lattice Γ in G, and μ_T the projection to G/Γ of normalized Haar measure on R_T, what is the limiting distribution of μ_T as T→∞?

evidence.quote: Let Γ be a lattice in G, and let µT denote the image of the normalized Haar measure on RT projected to G/Γ. QUESTION 20 (N. Shah) . What is the limiting distribution of the measure µT as T → ∞ ?

accepted.question_text: If α∈R is badly approximable by rationals, does the pair correlation R_2([a,b],N,α) for the sequence αn^2 mod 1 converge to b−a as N→∞?
accepted.context_brief: Pair correlations for quadratic Kronecker sequences

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 21 (Z. Rudnick, P . Sarnak). If α ∈ R is badly approximable by ratio-nals (see [218] for exact conditions), then (1) R2([a, b], N , α) → b − a as N → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For a continuous function f on T^1(X) with the stated cusp growth condition, badly approximable α∈R, and 0<c1<c2, do the averages M^{-1}∑_{m=1}^M f(u_y(αm)) converge uniformly to the Liouville integral as M→∞ for c1M^{-2}≤y≤c2M^{-2}?
accepted.context_brief: Discrete horocycle equidistribution at cusp scale

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 22 (J. Marklof, A. Strömbergsson) . Let f be a continuous function on T 1(X ) with given growth condition at the cusps (see [182]). Then for α ∈ R which is badly approximable by rationals and 0 < c1 < c2, 1 M M∑ m= 1 f (uy (αm)) → ∫ T1(X ) f d λ uniformly as M → ∞ and c1M − 2 ≤ y ≤ c2M − 2, where λ denotes the Liouville mea-sure.

accepted.question_text: For a finite-volume Riemannian locally symmetric space X of noncompact type, what is the asymptotic number of compact flats in X with volume less than T as T→∞?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 23 (H. Oh). Determine the asymptotics of the number of compact ﬂats with volume less than T as T → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For compact flats F⊂Γ\G with Vol(F)<T and measures ν_T and barν_T formed by volume-weighted and normalized averages over those flats, do ν_T and barν_T converge to normalized Haar measure on Γ\G?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 24 (H. Oh) . Do the measures νT and ¯νT converge to the normalized Haar measure on Γ\G?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a semisimple real algebraic group, Γ a noncocompact arithmetic lattice, and D a closed subgroup of a maximal R-split torus A. Are there no divergent D-orbits when dim D>rank_Q G, are all divergent trajectories obvious when dim D=rank_Q G, and do non-obvious divergent trajectories exist when dim D<rank_Q G?
accepted.context_brief: Divergent torus orbits in arithmetic quotients

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 25 (Barak Weiss). 1. If dim D > rankQG, then there are no diver-gent orbits of D. 2. If dim D = rankQG, then the only divergent trajectories are obvious ones. 3. If dim D < rankQG, then there are non-obvious divergent trajectories.

accepted.question_text: Can one construct examples of cones D in a maximal R-split torus A with dim D≥3 that have no non-obvious divergent trajectories?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 26 (Barak Weiss). Construct examples of cones D in A with dim D ≥ 3 and no non-obvious divergent trajectories.

accepted.question_text: Suppose dim A≥2 and x∈G/Γ is such that for every one-parameter subgroup D of A, the orbit Dx is not divergent in G/Γ. Must there exist a compact set K⊂G/Γ such that the limsup over T of the proportion of a in the radius-T ball A_T with ax∈K is positive?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 27 (Barak Weiss). Suppose that dim A ≥ 2 and for some x ∈ G/Γ and every one-parameter subgroup D of A, the orbits D x is not dive rgent in G /Γ. Is it true that there exists a compact set K ⊂ G/Γ such that lim sup T →∞ 1 λ(AT ) λ({a ∈ AT : ax ∈ K }) > 0?

accepted.question_text: Can analogs of geometric coding and arithmetic coding be constructed for the Weyl chamber flow, equivalently the diagonal group action, on SL(n,R)/SL(n,Z)?
accepted.context_brief: Symbolic coding for Weyl chamber flow

evidence.quote: QUESTION 28 (S. Katok). Construct analogs of the geometric coding and the arith-metic codings for the Weyl chamber ﬂow (i.e., the action the d iagonal group) on SL(n, R)/SL(n, Z).

accepted.question_text: Can periodic orbits be constructed for triangular billiards?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 29 (A. Katok). Construct periodic orbits for triangular billiards.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine modulo 2π and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 30 (A. Katok). Find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine (mod 2π) with ergodic (with respect to the Liouville measure) billia rd ﬂow.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a weakly mixing polygonal billiard; in particular, are Vorobets' billiards weakly mixing?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 31 (A. Katok) . Does there exist a weakly mixing polygonal billiard? Speciﬁcally, are Vorobets’ billiards [253] weakly mixing?

accepted.question_text: Does the set of ergodic billiard tables have positive measure?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 32 (A. Katok). Does the set of ergodic billiard tables have positive mea-sure?

accepted.question_text: For polygonal billiards, can one classify the ergodic invariant probability measures and the closed invariant subsets?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 33 (A. Katok). Classify the ergodic invariant probability measures and closed invariant subsets for polygonal billiards.

accepted.question_text: Let G be the direct product of k≥2 copies of SL(2,R), let U+ and U− be the upper and lower unipotent subgroups, and let Γ+ and Γ− be irreducible lattices in U+ and U−. If the group generated by Γ+ and Γ− is discrete, is it an arithmetic lattice in G?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 34 (G. Margulis, A. Selberg). If the group 〈Γ+ , Γ− 〉is discrete, then it is an arithmetic lattice in G.

accepted.question_text: Can one find reasonable and checkable conditions for a smooth map f:U⊂R^k→M_{m×n}(R) that generalize nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and imply that almost every point of f(U) is not very well approximable?
accepted.context_brief: Nondegenerate matrix-valued maps and VWA avoidance

evidence.quote: QUESTION 35 (D. Kleinbock, G. Margulis (see [144], Sec. 6.2)) . Find reasonable and checkable conditions for a smooth map f : U (⊂ Rk ) → Mm× n(R) which gener-alizes nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and implies tha t almost every point of f(U ) is not VWA.

accepted.question_text: Using dynamics, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable vectors lying in a nondegenerate submanifold of R^n?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable points on manifolds

evidence.quote: QUESTION 36 (D. Kleinbock). Give estimates of the Hausdorff dimension of v - approximable vectors in a nondegenerate submanifold of Rn using dynamics.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist real numbers α and β such that for every ε>0, liminf_{q→∞} q(log q)^{2−ε}⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ is positive?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 37 (A. Pollington). Are there α, β ∈ R such that for every ε > 0, lim infq→∞ q(log q)2− ε 〈qα〉 〈qβ〉> 0?

accepted.question_text: For every pair of real numbers α and β, is liminf_{q→∞} q⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ equal to 0, where ⟨x⟩ denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 38 (Littlewood). For any α, β ∈ R, lim inf q→∞ q 〈qα〉 〈qβ〉= 0.

accepted.question_text: Let A be the group of all diagonal matrices in SL(3,R). Is every bounded A-orbit in SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z) closed?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 39 (G. Margulis [174]) . Let A be the group of all diagonal matrices in SL(3, R). Then every bounded A-orbit in SL(3, R)/SL(3, Z) is closed.

accepted.question_text: For every compact set K in SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z), are there only finitely many closed A-orbits contained in K, where A is the full diagonal group in SL(3,R)?
accepted.context_brief: Finiteness of closed diagonal orbits in compact sets

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 40 (G. Margulis). For every compact set K of SL(3, R)/SL(3, Z), there are only ﬁnitely many closed A-orbits contained in K .

accepted.question_text: For every ε>0, is the set [ε,∞)∩{m(F)} finite, where m(F) is the normalized Markov minimum of a decomposable ternary form F?
accepted.context_brief: Finiteness in the Markov spectrum of decomposable forms

evidence.quote: QUESTION 41 (G. Margulis). Show that for every ε > 0, the set [ε, ∞ ) ∩ {m(F )} is ﬁnite.

accepted.question_text: For any s,t∈[0,1], is the intersection C_s∩C_t nonempty, where C_s consists of pairs (α,β) with inf_{q≥1} max{q^s⟨qα⟩, q^{1−s}⟨qβ⟩}>0?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 42 (W . Schmidt [226]). For any s , t ∈ [0, 1], we have Cs ∩ Ct ̸= /emptysetstress .

accepted.question_text: Let A be the group of all diagonal matrices in SL(3,R), and let A1 and A2 be rays in A. Does there exist x∈SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z) such that A1x and A2x are bounded but the full Ax orbit is not bounded?
accepted.context_brief: Two bounded diagonal rays without bounded full orbit

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 43. Let A be the group of all diagonal matrices in SL(3, R), and A1, A2 ⊂ A be rays in A. Then there exists x ∈ SL(3, R)/SL(3, Z) such that A 1x and A2x are bounded, but Ax is not bounded in SL(3, R)/SL(3, Z).

accepted.question_text: If Q is a nondegenerate positive definite quadratic form of dimension d≥3 that is not a multiple of a rational form, do the gaps between consecutive elements of {Q(x):x∈Z^d} go to zero as Q(x)→∞?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 44 (Davenport-Lewis). Suppose that Q is not a multiple of a ratio-nal form. Then the gaps between consecutive elements of the s et {Q(x) : x ∈ Zd } go to zero as Q (x) → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form Q of dimension d≥3 that is not a multiple of a rational quadratic form, can one give an effective estimate T=T(ε) guaranteeing an integer vector x∈Z^d with 0<|Q(x)|<ε and ||x||<T?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 45 (G. Margulis [174]) . Give an effective estimate on T = T (ε) such that there exists x ∈ Zd with 0 < | Q(x)| < ε and ∥x∥ < T.

accepted.question_text: For any nondegenerate indefinite binary quadratic form Q with rational coefficients that does not represent zero over Q, is the supremum m(Q) rational and isolated, and are both m(Q) and m2(Q) attained at points with coordinates in the splitting field of Q?
accepted.context_brief: Inhomogeneous minima of indefinite binary quadratic forms

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 46 (E. Barnes, H. Swinnerton-Dyer [11]). For any quadratic form Q as above, the supremum m(Q) is rational and isolated. Both m (Q) and m2(Q) are attained at points with coordinates in the the splitting ﬁel d of Q.

accepted.question_text: For B_s={(α,β)∈R^2: inf_{n≥1} n(min{||nα||,||nβ||})^s(max{||nα||,||nβ||})^{2−s}>0}, what is the Hausdorff dimension of B_s for 0<s<1?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of B_s Diophantine sets

evidence.quote: QUESTION 47 (Y . Bugeaud). Let Bs = { (α, β) ∈ R2 : inf n≥ 1 n(min{∥nα∥, ∥nβ∥})s(max{∥nα∥, ∥nβ∥})2− s > 0 } . Compute the Hausdorff dimension of the set Bs, 0 < s < 1.

accepted.question_text: In Katok's example of a Finsler metric on the two-dimensional sphere with ergodic geodesic flow and only two periodic orbits, do the closed geodesics correspond to scars?
accepted.context_brief: Scars in Katok's Finsler metric example

evidence.quote: QUESTION 48 (A. Katok) . Do the closed geodesics in this example correspond to scars?

accepted.question_text: If X has negative sectional curvature and μ_i are the probability measures |φ_i(x)|^2 dV(x) associated with Laplace eigenfunctions, does μ_i converge to dV as i→∞?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 49 (Quantum unique ergodicity). Suppose that X has negative sec-tional curvature. Then µi → dV as i → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For an arithmetic manifold with joint eigenfunctions of invariant differential operators and Hecke operators, is Riemannian volume the only arithmetic quantum limit?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 50 (Arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity). The Riemannian vol-ume is the only arithmetic quantum limit.

accepted.question_text: Let X=Γ\H^2 with Γ a noncocompact arithmetic lattice. For all compactly supported continuous functions f and g on X, does the ratio of their μ_i-integrals converge to the corresponding ratio of their Riemannian-volume integrals as i→∞?
accepted.context_brief: Nonescape ratio problem for arithmetic surfaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 51 (E. Lindenstrauss). Let X = Γ\H2 where Γ is a noncocompact arith-metic lattice. Show that for all f , g ∈ Cc (X ), ∫ X f d µi∫ X g d µi → ∫ X f dV∫ X g dV as i → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For generic negatively curved compact Riemannian manifolds, do Laplace eigenfunctions φ_i have Gaussian value distribution, so that Vol({x∈X:a≤φ_i(x)≤b}) converges to (1/√(2π))∫_a^b exp(−t^2/2)dt as i→∞?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 52 (J. Marklof ). Vol({x ∈ X : a ≤ φi (x) ≤ b}) → 1/rad〉callow 2π ∫ b a e − t 2/2d t as i → ∞ .

accepted.question_text: For generic negatively curved compact Riemannian manifolds X and a∈C_c^∞(S^*X,R) with Liouville mean zero, does ξ_i(a)=λ_i^{1/4}|⟨Op(a)φ_i,φ_i⟩| have a Gaussian limiting distribution with variance V(a)=∫_{−∞}^{∞}∫_{S^*X}a(xg^t)a(x)dλ(x)dt, including convergence of second moments and interval counts as stated?
accepted.context_brief: Central limit theorem for quantum variance

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 53 (J. Marklof, after Feingold-Peres [73]) . Suppose X is “generic”. For a ∈ C ∞ c (S ∗ X , R) with ∫ S∗ X a dλ = 0, put ξi (a) = λ1/4 i ⏐ ⏐〈Op(a)φi , φi 〉 ⏐ ⏐ . Then the sequence ξi (a) has a Gaussian limit distribution whose variance is given by the classical autocorrelation function V (a) := ∫ ∞ −∞ ∫ S∗ X a(xg t )a(x) d λ(x)d t. That is, as λ → ∞ , 1. 1 λ ∑ λi ≤ λ ξi (a)2 → V (a), 2. for any interval I ∈ R 1 λ # { λi ≤ λ : V (a)− 1/2ξi (a) ∈ I } → 1/rad〉callow 2π ∫ I e − t 2/2d t.

accepted.question_text: Do periodic orbits in a triangular billiard correspond to scars; more precisely, are there quantum limits supported on periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 54 (A. Katok). Do periodic orbits in a triangular billiard correspond to scars? More precisely, are there quantum limits supported on periodic orbits?

accepted.question_text: Can one classify all quantum limits of eigenfunctions of a polygonal billiard?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 55 (J. Marklof ). Classify all quantum limits of the eigenfunctions of a polygonal billiard.

accepted.question_text: For a positive definite quadratic form Q on Z^2, what is the distribution of pairs (Q(x1)−Q(x2), Q(x2)−Q(x3)) with distinct xi∈Z^2? More precisely, what are the asymptotics of N_T((a,b),(c,d)) counting triples with a<Q(x1)−Q(x2)<b, c<Q(x2)−Q(x3)<d, distinct xi, and ||xi||<T?
accepted.context_brief: Triple spacing distribution for quadratic-form values

evidence.quote: QUESTION 56 (J. Marklof ). What is the distribution of the set {(Q(x1) − Q(x2),Q(x2) − Q(x3)) : xi ∈ Z2, xi ̸= x j for i ̸= j } ⊂ R2? More precisely, determine the asymptotics of NT ((a, b), (c, d )) := # { (x1, x2, x3) ∈ (Z2)3 : a < Q(x1) − Q(x2) < b, c < Q(x2) − Q(x3) < d , xi ̸= x j for i ̸= j , ∥xi ∥ < T }.

accepted.question_text: Is the Zariski closure of any set of special points in a Shimura variety a finite union of special subvarieties?
